name: Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design
visualIdentity: A dark technical interface with fine wireframes, readable monospaced data, and restrained cyan or magenta accents. Panels, reticles, scales, maps, and rings should serve clear functions; label fictional data. This is a descriptive interface direction, not a requirement to make every cyberpunk scene a HUD.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to fictional interfaces and title sequences. With meaningful data, it can support operations dashboards, mission-control reports, tech trailers, audio or sensor diagnostics, and interactive HTML dashboards. These are inferred uses from the supplied combinations.
limitations: Avoid meaningless microtext, excessive spinning rings, overexposed neon, and readouts that animate without corresponding events. Preserve data meaning and readability. Exploded reveals suit only separable components whose relationships they explain. Interactive hover and scroll behavior needs accessible equivalents and reduced-motion handling.
palette: Use a dominant dark background, clear foreground hierarchy, and one limited cyan accent; magenta is an approved alternative, not an automatic addition. Suggested fallback tokens for new artwork only: background #0C1822, foreground #E7F4F3, accent #55C7CF. These are not canonical: supplied, brand, and source colors take precedence. Keep colors discrete; no gradient is enabled. Bloom is selective, and actual composited contrast must be checked.
motionAndInteraction: Synchronize startup, scanning, acquisition, and feedback with visible data events. Use smooth coherent movement where helpful, while preserving purposeful impacts, cuts, and reading holds. For video, derive states from seekable composition time and ensure direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks render correctly. For HTML, pointer tilt, reversible hotspot reveals, and scroll-driven chapters or stories are optional; provide focus or touch behavior and stable reverse states.
audio: No soundtrack is mandated. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Do not imply playback, waveforms, or spatial panning without real audio. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping, and synchronize audio and picture.
assetRequirements: Use supplied assets, exact copy, palettes, and authorized audio as given. Build wireframe or point-line 3D forms with SVG or HTML scales and text; use readable labels and real data where applicable. Prepare and load fonts and assets before rendering. Maps need valid geographic data, attribution, and authorized sources; graphs need validated relationships. Do not present simulated appearances as physical production.
combinations: Can stand alone. With style-097, meaningful charts or maps can occupy HUD panels; keep charts accurate, accents restrained, and every animated readout tied to data. With style-063, bounded cyan waveforms can signal audio or sensor activity; avoid full-screen traces and distracting CRT effects. Motion-017 is compatible only for explanatory component separation. Other listed motion patterns are optional when their chapter or story progression fits the content; none is required.
productionApproach: Select style rendering and motion tools for fidelity and scene needs; Three.js handles genuine 3D, SVG scales and masks, D3 data layouts, and selective bloom highlights. Use one owner per animated property and deterministic time-driven state. HyperFrames is the primary composition, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output, and record why. Tools listed are options, not a required bundle.
